concepts.def: Emile Durkheim's Elementary Forms 1912: 'unified system of beliefs and practices relative to sacred things'; functionalist sociological approach.
Judaism, Christianity, Islam; trace descent from Abraham; monotheistic; share Hebrew Bible/Torah and ethical monotheism.
Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism originating in Indian subcontinent; share karma, dharma and rebirth concepts.
Chinese family including Daoism, Confucianism and folk religion; emphasise harmony, yin-yang and ancestor veneration.
Ninian Smart's Seven Dimensions of Religion 1989: doctrinal, mythical, ethical, ritual, experiential, social, material.
Friedrich Max Muller's 1870 founding of comparative religion at Royal Institution; 'he who knows one knows none'.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An Introduction to the Acts of the Apostles — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

An Introduction to the Acts of the Apostles brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with An Introduction to the Acts of the Apostles.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
